- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope to reflect mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is positive but model forecast is consistently below true outcome, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 2-5% for the next 3-5 days.  
- Model frequently underestimates true price in the first 5-7 days of a new 30d horizon; apply a 1-3% upward bias to early forecast points.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to lag true price by 1-3 days; shift forecast forward by 1-2 days and adjust magnitude to match sentiment direction.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; add a 2-5% downward correction to forecast from peak onward.
